portion_doctrine: Segments 1-10 are 95% Gemini chat navigation clutter + sidebar boilerplate. Real content appears starting ~25% through: a strategic business blueprint for separating SNIPED Media (B2C cash machine) from Baseplate (B2B/wellness operator toolkit). Core thesis: two separate operational lanes, zero bleed, distinct revenue stacks, pricing-as-gatekeeper. Baseplate's core product is a $47 Direction Stack manual (protocol reference guide for photographers fixing biomechanics/tension on set). Secondary revenue: $15 field guide upsell, $97-497 workshop tier, future AR SaaS. Implementation is hyper-specific: Pixieset integration, 3-tier pricing ($275/$550+/$custom event quotes), Intake form questionnaires, automated booking/payment gatekeeping, contract templates, visual directives. Brand/voice doctrine: 'highly competent, reliable local professional.' Typography system locked (Space Grotesk + 1 paired sans). The document is a raw working session: half strategic clarity, half tactical implementation notes. Actionable gold is the 7-figure D2C playbook (wage separation, volume capping, gallery upsells, seasonal constraints, document-over-create content strategy) and the Pixieset field-by-field configuration specs.
operating_rules: Wage Separation: Pool business revenue, pay fixed weekly salary, reinvest remaining profit. Distinct from personal spend.
Volume Cap: Set hard limits per season (e.g., 'grad season only' or fixed shoots/month). Prevent burnout and margin collapse.
One-time Deliverable: Post-shoot revision cycles end at contract boundary. No endless back-and-forth. Standardized packages.
Gallery Upsell on Every Shoot: Deliver contract-required images only. Sell remaining gallery at full margin via password-protected Pixieset hosting.
Document, Don't Create: Content strategy is behind-the-scenes documentation, not original creative. Mundane posts perform.
No Bleeding Lanes: SNIPED Media (B2C events/portraits) and Baseplate (B2B/operator wellness) run completely separate operational boxes. Same playbook failure leads to dilution and exhaustion.
Calendar is the Rule Enforcer: Pixieset availability settings strictly control when clients can book. No manual exceptions (exceptions break automation).
Price for Evidence, Not Wishful Thinking: Charge based on proven results and case studies. V1 is lower price, V2 raises after social proof exists.
Zero Friction After Commitment: Confirmation messaging, contract, and questionnaire must feel like a single integrated flow, not admin burden.
Intake Form Gatekeeping: Pixieset's intake form automatically rejects leads below tier threshold. No manual review of low-budget inquiries.
Uncheck Offline Payment: Stripe-only for Tier 1/2. Checking 'Cash/Venmo' option destroys automated payment enforcement.
Split Contract Templates: Tier 1 contract separate from Tier 2/3. A $275 session contract shouldn't reference $550+ payment terms. Avoid confusion and looks generic.
Pre-Attached Visual Directive: Questionnaires auto-attached to intake form. Don't send manually. Visual Directive answers stored in project.
Cancellation & Rescheduling Clarity: Explicit in contract. How far in advance, what they forfeit, how many reschedules allowed.
Expert Direction Phrasing: Build trust through confident, specific language. 'Expert Direction' pulls from competence without over-teaching.
Brand Voice Anchor: Sound like 'highly competent, reliable local professional who has their business completely together.' Specific, confident, not flashy.
Header CTA Singular Focus: Only one routing button in header (Book/Inquire/Check Availability). No email link, no phone. Eliminate friction paths.
No Pixieset Print Store for Baseplate: Turn off studio merchandise. '7-figure D2C founder does not sell trinkets.' Boundaries protect brand integrity.
Maximum Advance Booking: 60 days. Prevents calendar lock-up before you know travel/event schedule.
Availability Window (Tier 1): Saturday 9am-2pm, Sunday 12pm-5pm. Block all weekday slots (non-negotiable, you're at W-2 job).
Tier 1 Duration: 45 minutes. Tier 2: 90 minutes. Explicit time boundary protects labor economics.
Tier 1 Retouched Deliverable: 5 retouched images per contract. Additional images sold via gallery at full markup.
Tier 2 Retouched Deliverable: 15 retouched images per contract (90-minute session scaling).
Payment Split Option (Tier 2): 50% upfront retainer ($137.50), balance 50% due 48 hours before shoot. Eliminates day-of payment friction.
Two-Reschedule Maximum: Prevents endless rescheduling and calendar churn.
Contact Auto-Creation: When payment received, contact auto-created in Pixieset CRM. 30-second manual entry.
Field Validation on Pixieset Intake: Phone (required), Headcount (number field, required), Wardrobe description (long text, required), Date confirmation (date field).
Tier 3 Is Custom Quote Only: No booking button. Direct to sales flow. Events require bespoke pricing and approval gate.
named_methods: Lead Magnet + Email Nurture + Upsell Sequence
specific_tactics: Session name: 'The Moment | Portrait Session' (Tier 1), 'The Statement | Signature Session' (Tier 2). Tier-specific naming signals value differential.
Hero image for booking page: Single subject portrait only (Sasha headshot or strong Nubian x Joi campaign image). No group shots or event photos.

Pixieset booking flow: Form capture on /book → 24-hour follow-up email with custom quote → Pixieset Studio Manager contact creation → Quote link to contract → Retainer payment → Questionnaire link → Calendar scheduling → Gallery creation.
Formspree backup role: Captures form submission (you get email notification), but primary routing is to Pixieset booking links. Acts as silent cart recovery.

Intake form field progression: Name/email (locked default) → Phone (required) → Headcount (number, required) → Wardrobe description (long text, required) → Contract & Questionnaire (pre-attached, auto-deploy).
Confirmation message (post-payment, tier-agnostic): 'Got it. I'll follow up within 24 hours with your custom scope and quote.' Emphasizes immediate high-touch follow-up.
Contract variable binding: Contract auto-populates client name, session date, and fee amount from booking payload.
Tier 2 payment reminder: Pixieset auto-sends balance reminder 48 hours before shoot (no manual tracking needed).
Tier 3 event flow: Quote request → Custom quote generation in Pixieset → Separate contract per event → Approval gate before calendar lock.
Gumroad page for $47 manual: Separate storefront for physical deliverable (PDF). Not hosted on main Sniped/Baseplate sites.
Lead magnet sequence: Protocol 01 free (email capture) → Nurture sequence → Upsell full $47 manual → $15 field guide bump at checkout.
Questionnaire timing: Send after payment + contract signature. Pre-built template in Pixieset, no manual email trigger.
Typography pairing: Space Grotesk (bold/semibold) for headings. Paired with a secondary sans (likely Inter or similar for body). No serif mixing.
Metadata SEO: Include meta descriptions, og:image (work-portraits.jpg, work-lifestyle.jpg, work-events.jpg). Hero + Work Teaser imagery embedded.
CTA button singular: Header contains only one routing button. All CTAs flow to /book page first, then to Pixieset intake or calendar depending on tier.
Email domain for Studio Manager: admin@snipedmedia.com authenticated for Drive/Calendar/admin. Personal Google account is temporary bridge only.
prompts: Prompt for Claude Code (Next.js booking integration): 'Disregard the previous logic regarding the booking flow. Sniped Media is a [Baseplate/SNIPED Media] build. Help me optimize this in my system we've been building so I build it with more context. Here's exactly what to do. I'm walking you through this step by step based on the actual Pixieset documentation. Do each one as I describe it.' [Then paste Pixieset field-by-field configuration specs]

Prompt for Pixieset Session Type Creation: 'I'm setting up two Session Types in Pixieset Studio Manager right now. I need you to give me the exact content for each field the client sees, the field type (text, dropdown, number, multi-select, date, etc.) based on what Pixieset questionnaires support, and tell me exactly what to enter or select at each step.' [Then provide tier-specific answers]
Prompt for Visual Directive Questionnaire: [Pre-built template in Pixieset, auto-attached to intake form, no manual prompt needed. Captures wardrobe, lighting preference, mood, subject history.]
tools: Pixieset Studio Manager (CRM, booking, invoicing, gallery hosting, contracts, questionnaires, calendar)
Formspree (form capture on /book page, email notification backup)
SavvyCal or Calendly (diagnostic call booking, embedded in footer)
Adobe Lightroom (post-production editing, assumed existing workflow)
content_ideas: Direction Stack Manual ($47): 58-page PDF covering 10 complete protocols for fixing biomechanics/tension on set. Includes verbal cues and prevention sequences. Positioned as 'end of guessing.' MVP for Baseplate brand.
Field Guide ($15 upsell): Companion tool, positioned as tactical reference. Sold at checkout after $47 purchase decision.
Free Protocol 01 Lead Magnet: One complete protocol (e.g., 'Claw Hands' or 'Spinal Collapse') given free in exchange for email. Trust mechanism and data collection.
Before/After Frames: Case studies showing photographers using protocols to save failing shoots. Social proof for V2 pricing justification.
Video Demonstrations: Short clips showing how each protocol prevents common posing failures. Content for email nurture sequence.
Operator's Kit (future V2, $150-250): Bundled product with reviews, before/after video library, all 10 protocols, and workshopping rights. Priced after social proof accumulates.
AR Tool Vision (Future SaaS Phase): 'Point phone at subject, AI reads biomechanics, flags tension, suggests protocol.' Future product after manual validation data is collected.
Behind-the-Scenes Documentation (SNIPED): Post mundane, non-polished process photos. Authenticates the business.
Gallery Upsell Marketing: Email sequence post-shoot positioning additional images as 'unseen moments from your session.' Sell at perceived-value pricing.
Baseplate Case Studies: Document photographers who used protocols to level-up their work. Feature before/after frames and quotes.
contradictions: Price anchoring conflict: Document says V1 should be low ($47) to accumulate proof, but also states 'price for evidence not wishful thinking.' This creates chicken-egg risk: proof requires case studies, case studies require customers, customers want proof. Strategy mitigates with free Protocol 01 as trust mechanism.

Volume cap vs. scaling tension: Operating rule says 'set hard volume limits' to prevent burnout, but future vision is 'venture-backed tech platform.' Hard caps conflict with growth-hacking mentality. Resolution: Baseplate (manual/toolkit) and SNIPED (events/portraits) are separate lanes; caps apply to SNIPED only.

Two-lane separation vs. shared infrastructure: Document says 'keep in strict operational box so it doesn't drain energy,' but both use Pixieset, Stripe, same Next.js app. Infrastructure bleeds even if operational lanes don't. Risk: admin overhead still aggregates.

Manual touchpoint automation: Document claims 'frictionless automation,' but requires manual contact entry in Pixieset (30 seconds), manual quote generation, and manual follow-up email. 'Automated' is UI-level, not back-end.

Brand voice vs. Baseplate persona mismatch: SNIPED voice is 'calm, quiet luxury, editorial restraint' per memory. Baseplate voice is 'highly competent, reliable local professional.' These are compatible but not identical. Risk: cross-brand messaging dilution if not disciplined.
weird_gold: The $47 pricing insight: At $47 you need 64 sales to hit $3k revenue. At $19 you need 158 sales. Jumping to $19 is NOT half the work; it's 2.5x the customers, 2.5x the reviews to manage, 2.5x the support questions, 2.5x the refund risk. This inverts common 'lower price = bigger market' logic.

'End of guessing' as the core value prop: The manual doesn't sell protocols or pages. It sells certainty on set. Single-sentence pitch: 'The end of guessing.' This is the leverage point for all downstream upsells.

Gallery upsell as the real margin engine: Shoot 25 images, deliver 5 in contract, sell 20 at full retail margin. The session fee ($275/$550) is the lead magnet. Gallery upsell is where actual profit lives.
Tier naming as psychological anchoring: 'The Moment' (singular, intimate) vs. 'The Statement' (group, formal, significant). Names telegraph scope without saying headcount.

Expert Direction phrasing as trust without teaching: 'Pulling lightly from the fact that you know how to fix physical tension, without over-teaching the protocols.' This reserves IP (full protocols only in paid manual) while building credibility.
Pixieset as the 5-tool consolidation: Replaces gallery hosting + print fulfillment + CRM + invoicing + contracts + scheduling. Single integration point eliminates tool fatigue.

The 'no bleeding lanes' doctrine as burnout prevention: Explicit operational separation (not just conceptual) prevents decision fatigue. Different processes, different platforms (ideally), different audience. This is anti-scale thinking as exhaustion management.

Cancellation & rescheduling as contractual gatekeeping: Explicit limits (e.g., '2 reschedules maximum, 48-hour cancellation window') eliminate endless back-and-forth. Contracts enforce operational boundaries.

The $15 field guide timing: Sold at the point of maximum commitment (post-payment, pre-send). Frictionless upsell because buyer already validated with $47 decision. Same mechanism as impulse checkout items.

Protocol 01 free as data collection engine: Manual is MVP, but free protocol is the real product-market fit validator. If photographers use free protocol and save a shoot, they've already felt the ROI before paying.
gates: Tier threshold gate: Pixieset intake form auto-rejects any lead selecting budget under tier minimum. No manual review path for low-budget inquiries.
Tier 3 approval gate: Custom event quotes require explicit go/no-go decision before contract is sent. Prevents over-commitment to low-margin work.
Payment enforcement gate: Stripe-only. If 'Offline Payment' is checked, gate fails because clients can book without swiping card, destroying automation.
Contract signature gate: Questionnaire + calendar lock only available after contract is signed and payment received. Prevents qualified-inquiry abandonment.
Advance booking gate: 60-day maximum. Prevents calendar lock-up beyond visibility horizon.
Visual Directive gate: Questionnaire response required before pre-shoot communication. Ensures client brief is captured and stored.
48-Hour Balance Due Gate (Tier 2): Auto-reminder sent. Session prep doesn't start until balance is received.
Interview/Screening gate for case studies (future): Only document photographers who use protocols on real-paid shoots. No toy projects. Ensures credibility of before/afters.
Copywriting gate: All positioning language must pass 'Expert Direction' test. Avoid over-teaching, protect protocol IP.
